paginas.titulo: Golden dorado fishing trip with friends: how many days, how much it costs, and where to stay (2026/27)
paginas.bajada: Three ways to plan a golden dorado trip with friends on the Paraná: per-person prices for each, what's included, and how many days are best.
paginas.seo_title: Golden dorado fishing trip with friends: 2026/27 prices
paginas.seo_description: How much a golden dorado fishing trip with friends in Argentina costs: from US$ 605 per person at an inn to US$ 4,050 at a lodge. Days and what's included.
datos: Inn in Esquina (Corrientes): 2 fishing days and 3 nights from US$ 605 per person in a group of three and from US$ 705 in a group of two, with meals, boat, guide, and license.
Houseboat in the Paraná Delta: 3 nights from US$ 1,260 and 4 nights from US$ 1,680 per person.
All-inclusive lodge in Corrientes: 3 nights and 2 fishing days from US$ 4,050 per person; 7 nights and 6 days US$ 7,950.
The more days, the cheaper each fishing day: at an inn in Esquina, it drops from US$ 353 to US$ 326 per person between 2 and 4 days.
The extraordinary fishing ban on the Paraná in Corrientes was lifted on 29 September 2026.

bloques.h: Short answer. For a dorado trip with friends, it's best to go for 2 to 4 fishing days. The per-person price depends more on the type of lodging than the number of days: from US$ 605 to US$ 705 at an inn (2 fishing days, 3 nights), from US$ 1,260 on a Delta houseboat, and from US$ 4,050 at an all-inclusive lodge. All prices are per person, in US dollars, not including travel.
Three ways to do it, with prices

filas: Lodging, meals, drinks, boat, guide, bait, fuel, and license
Same, with the price split among three
Double lodging, all meals and drinks, guide, and loaner gear
Same; does not include license, transfers, or travel

bloques.h: Prices published or reported as of 5 November 2026, per person in double room and shared guide. Each lodge's rates by number of nights are in how much a golden dorado fishing trip costs.
How many days are best for a dorado trip with friends?

Our opinion, based on published numbers: 3 nights and 2 fishing days if time is short, since a windy or rainy day matters less than on a one-day trip; and 4 nights and 3 days if you're traveling from far away, as the cost per fishing day drops and travel is already paid. At an inn in Esquina, the per-person, per-fishing-day cost goes from US$ 353 (2 days) to US$ 337 (3 days) and US$ 326 (4 days), for a group of two. These are our calculations.
Multi-day packages at an inn in Esquina

Posada Hambaré, National Route 12, km 688, Esquina. "From" prices as of 4 November 2026; the inn does not publish the season for these rates. Includes lodging; breakfast, lunch, and dinner; soft drinks, water, beer, and unlimited wine; boat, fishing guide, two dozen live baits per person, 50 liters of fuel, and fishing license. Totals and cost per fishing day are our calculations.
How much for your group?
Our calculation, not including travel or gear. For 4 and 6 friends, you need to confirm the inn has two boats available on your dates and that each group keeps its price.
What if you prefer a one-day trip?

A guide in Esquina advertises a full day on the boat with guide from $ 480,000 per boat, or $ 160,000 per person if there are three (1 November 2026, in pesos). In Paso de la Patria, none of the operators we checked publish a day rate: offers say "all inclusive" or "inquire." We do not set the exchange rate between pesos and dollars: confirm it when booking.
Is there a fishing ban on the Paraná in Corrientes now?

filas: Order 618: ban between km 1232 and 1238, due to a concentration of surubí
Extended to km 1180 to 1239, Paso de la Patria jurisdiction, for dorado and sábalo
Order 1054: ban lifted and regulations from Order 853/22 reinstated

bloques.h: Corrientes Department of Natural Resources. We found no ban after 4 November 2026, but the rules allow it to be reinstated if fish concentrations reappear: ask your guide before heading out. Since Order 853/22, dorado and surubí must be released in Corrientes.
Do I need a fishing license?

Yes. In Corrientes, you get the sport fishing license online and carry it with your ID. It's already included in Esquina inn packages and some lodges; in others, it's not (the Corrientes lodges in the nights table do not include it). Always ask.
Want help planning? Tell us your dates, number of friends, and budget in the trip form and we'll send you guide and lodging options, free of charge and with no obligation.
What this page doesn't cover yet
Bus and flight schedules from Buenos Aires, the Corrientes license price, and a month-by-month calendar with technical sources. We'll add them once we verify with a date.

items: The fishing license: in Corrientes you get it online; some lodges include it, others don't.

Full day on the Limay: from US$ 500 (one angler) and US$ 520 (two) with one outfitter, US$ 530 with another and from US$ 545 with an agency.
Full day on the Manso: US$ 600, which includes a US$ 70 supplement over the Limay.

bloques.h: Short answer. A day of guided fly fishing near Bariloche costs from US$ 410 for a half day and from US$ 500 for a full day, per boat for one or two anglers. The Manso goes up to US$ 600. In pesos, a guide on a platform lists $ 666,000 per day. These are entry prices: what changes the price is below. The license is paid separately.
Prices by trip type

filas: Private guide and boat, gear, transfers, snack
From US$ 500 one angler, US$ 520 two (one outfitter); US$ 530 (another outfitter); from US$ 545 (an agency)
Guide, boat, gear, transfers, lunch and drinks

bloques.h: Prices published or reported as of 6 November 2026, per boat with guide and for one or two anglers. The prices in dollars and pesos are from different operators and are not converted between each other: each sets their own exchange rate at booking.
Why are there so many prices?

Because published prices are entry level, not a cap. They change with the river (the Manso adds US$ 70 to the Limay), with duration (half day is US$ 410 and full day from US$ 500) and with what each operator includes. Some operators also offer multi-day programs and float trips with camping and do not publish rates: you have to ask. We also did not find a published rate above US$ 600 for a day; others may charge more, but we can't confirm it without a published price.
How much for two anglers?

The price is per boat, not per person. With the outfitter who lists both rates, one angler pays US$ 500 and two anglers in the same boat pay US$ 520 total: the second adds only US$ 20. Per person, going as a pair is almost half (our calculation: US$ 260 per person). With the full day on the Limay at US$ 530, it's US$ 265 per person.
How much is the fishing license?

The Patagonian permit is valid in Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut and National Parks, and its 2026/27 rates are official, in pesos: non-resident foreigners, $ 50,000 per day, $ 140,000 for 10 days and $ 280,000 for the season; residents, $ 12,500, $ 25,000 and $ 50,000 (regulations updated 26 October 2026). Some operators handle it for you and charge it separately: one reports US$ 40 per person per day. All rates, who is exempt and the trolling permit are in Patagonia fishing license 2026/27.
When is the best time to go?
A local outfitter says the best time is November to May. This is one outfitter's description; the official season and closures are in our Patagonia trout season guide.

paginas.titulo: Patagonian Argentina Fishing License 2026/27: Cost and Validity
paginas.bajada: Official prices for the Patagonian fishing permit for the 2026/27 season, for foreigners and residents, where it's valid, duration, and extra fees.
paginas.seo_description: How much is the Patagonia fishing permit 2026/27: foreigners ARS 50,000 per day and ARS 280,000 for the season; neighboring countries, 10 days at ARS 50,000.
datos: Non-resident foreigners: ARS 50,000 per day, ARS 140,000 for 10 days, and ARS 280,000 for the season (2026/27 rates, in pesos).
Residents in Argentina: ARS 12,500 per day, ARS 25,000 for 10 days, and ARS 50,000 for the season.
The same permit is valid in Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut, and the Southern National Parks; Santa Cruz and Tierra del Fuego have their own.
The fishing season runs from 1 November 2026 to 1 May 2027 inclusive; the season permit is valid until 31 October 2027.
No charge: people over 65, retirees, pensioners, children up to 12 years old, and people with disabilities with official accreditation.
Río Negro also sells a 10-day permit for non-resident foreigners from neighboring countries (including Brazil) at ARS 50,000; this is a provincial category and only valid in the issuing province.

bloques.h: Short answer. To fish in Argentine Patagonia during the 2026/27 season, a non-resident foreigner pays ARS 50,000 for one day, ARS 140,000 for 10 days, or ARS 280,000 for the season, and a resident pays ARS 12,500, ARS 25,000, or ARS 50,000. The permit is the same in Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut, and the Southern National Parks.
Permit prices 2026/27

filas: Non-resident foreigner from neighboring country (provincial category, Río Negro)

bloques.h: Prices in Argentine pesos from the General Regulations for Patagonian Continental Sport Fishing, text updated 26 October 2026. Read on 6 November 2026. Dollar value varies with the daily exchange rate.
Is there a cheaper permit for neighboring countries?

Yes, in Río Negro. Its official sales page includes the permit for non-resident foreigners from neighboring countries, 10 days, at ARS 50,000 (code E-L10), compared to ARS 140,000 for the regular 10-day foreign permit. This can be used, for example, by residents of Brazil, Chile, Uruguay, Paraguay, or Bolivia. It is a provincial category: the regulations state that permits in categories not listed in the common table are only valid in the jurisdiction that issues them, so this is valid in Río Negro and not in Neuquén, Chubut, or the National Parks. The price list for Chubut published by Aire Libre magazine also includes it; confirm on Chubut's sales page before relying on it.
Who doesn't pay for the permit?

No permit fee for people over 65, retirees and pensioners, children up to 12 years old, and people with disabilities with official accreditation (resident category). Minors aged 13 to 17 pay ARS 25,000 for the season.
Where is the Patagonian permit valid?

Permits issued by Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut, and the National Parks Administration, with these categories and prices, are the only ones valid for fishing in all waters of those four jurisdictions. Each province also has annexes with exceptions for specific rivers and lakes: check them before fishing a particular water. Santa Cruz and Tierra del Fuego do not use this permit: they have their own, with different prices (see guides for {d:rio-gallegos} and {d:rio-grande}).
How long is the permit valid and when is the season?

items: Fishing season: from 1 November 2026 to 1 May 2027 inclusive. Each province's annexes have exceptions (waters that open or close on other dates).
Season permit: valid from the date of issue until 31 October 2027.
One-day and 10-day permits: valid for the dates indicated on the permit.
Hours: fishing is only allowed during daylight hours.

bloques.h: What do I need to bring?

The permit is personal and non-transferable, must be fully completed, and you must carry and show it whenever requested by authorities, along with an ID. In Chubut, the digital permit managed through the DINO platform can be re-downloaded for free if lost.
How much is the permit for a one-week trip?

For a foreigner fishing 6 to 7 days, the 10-day permit (ARS 140,000) is cheaper than six daily permits (ARS 300,000) and cheaper than the season permit (ARS 280,000) if not returning. This is our calculation based on the prices above; lodge week prices on our pages indicate if the license is included: see how much a week of trout fishing in Neuquén and Chubut costs and a day of fishing in Bariloche.

paginas.titulo: Fishing in Corrientes from Brazil: license, documents, routes & costs (2026/27)
paginas.bajada: Which license an angler coming from Brazil needs, approximate cost, what documents to bring, and travel times to Paso de la Patria, Esquina, and Goya.
paginas.seo_title: Fishing Corrientes from Brazil: license & how to get there
paginas.seo_description: How to fish in Corrientes coming from Brazil: foreign tourist license (from about $ 35,000 per day), entry documents, and routes with travel times.
datos: The foreign tourist license (residence outside Argentina) is set in liters of “súper” gasoline (the standard grade, not premium): 16 liters for one day, 20 for two, 24 for three, 28 for four, and 36 for six.
With “súper” gasoline at about $ 2,177 per liter, that's approximately $ 35,000 for one day, $ 44,000 for two, $ 52,000 for three, $ 61,000 for four, and $ 78,000 for six.
The license is obtained online, 24 hours a day, and the portal is available in Spanish, English, and Portuguese; the registration accepts the Brazilian CPF as a document.
To enter Argentina from Brazil you need a physical RG in good condition or a valid passport; digital versions and driver's license (CNH) are not accepted.
From Uruguaiana to Esquina is 310 km (4 h 31 min) and from São Borja to Paso de la Patria, 386 km (4 h 45 min), according to Google Maps.

fuentes.nombre: Disposición 1144/2024, Dirección de Recursos Naturales de Corrientes (27 de septiembre de 2024): types, liters, and license values
Pump prices from the Secretaría de Energía: average “súper” gasoline price at 14 Corrientes stations (21 October 2026)
License portal of the Dirección de Recursos Naturales de Corrientes: registration (read on 6 November 2026)
Corrientes Ministry of Tourism: online licenses in three languages (note from 6 February 2019)
Paso Santo Tomé - São Borja, National Security Ministry
Official tourism site of Argentina: entry documents (28 October 2026)
Google Maps: routes by car checked on 6 November 2026

bloques.h: Short answer. To fish in Corrientes, a Brazilian needs the foreign tourist license, which is obtained online and paid in pesos based on the price of “súper” gasoline. Today it costs about $ 35,000 for one day, $ 52,000 for three days, and $ 78,000 for six. To enter, a physical RG in good condition or a passport is enough. From Uruguaiana to Esquina is about 310 km and 4 h 30 min driving.
How much does a fishing license in Corrientes cost for a foreigner?

The liters are from Annex I of Disposición 1144/2024 of the Dirección de Recursos Naturales de Corrientes. The value is updated only with the price of “súper” gasoline sold at the Automóvil Club Argentino in Corrientes Capital: the annex used $ 1,135 per liter in October 2024. We calculated today's approximate value with $ 2,177 per liter, which is the average at 14 Corrientes stations according to pump prices from the Secretaría de Energía (updated 21 October 2026). It's not the exact ACA price: the portal shows the current amount at purchase.
Is it worth getting a multi-day license?

Yes. Each extra day costs less: the 3-day license (24 liters) is half the price of three one-day licenses (48 liters, about $ 104,000), and the 6-day license (36 liters) is just over a third of six one-day licenses (96 liters). This is our calculation using the table's liters.
How do you get the license online?

items: On the portal of the Dirección de Recursos Naturales de Corrientes. It's available 24 hours and in Spanish, English, and Portuguese, according to the provincial Ministry of Tourism (2019 note, made for Brazilian tourism).
Registration requires type and ID number, email, first and last name, phone, location, profile photo, and password.
Document: the registration dropdown offers DNI, Brazilian CPF, Uruguayan CI, Argentine passport, and "Others" (screenshot from 6 November 2026).
The license has a QR code that the inspector checks with a phone. Bring it, printed or on your phone, on the boat.

bloques.h: We couldn't confirm which payment methods the portal accepts for foreigners: ask the Dirección de Recursos Naturales (ventas@recnaturalesctes.gob.ar or +54 379 4909039). The exemption benefits in the regulation (retirees, people with disabilities, under 15) apply only to those with residence in Corrientes.
What documents do I need to enter Argentina from Brazil?

items: Physical RG in good condition or valid passport. Digital versions are not accepted, including digital RG.
CNH is not valid as an entry document.
Under 13 years old: need a special authorization; see the process at argentina.gob.ar ("entering the country with a minor").
Some guides and lodges recommend an RG less than 10 years old: this is practical advice, not an official requirement.

bloques.h: According to Argentina's official tourism site, checked on 28 October 2026. Confirm with Immigration before traveling.
How long does it take from the border?

filas: São Borja (Brazil) → Paso de la Patria

bloques.h: Google Maps times checked on 6 November 2026; do not include border wait. The Santo Tomé - São Borja crossing, via the International Integration Bridge, is open 24 hours (National Security Ministry; phone (3756) 420035).
Where to fish and how much does the trip cost?

paginas.seo_title: What’s included in an Argentina fishing package
paginas.seo_description: What’s included and what’s extra in Argentina fishing packages: license, transfers, flights, single room, tips, with 2026/27 examples.
datos: In nine published packages for 2026/27, the fishing license is included in 4, excluded in 3, and 2 don’t specify.
None of the packages that specify include international flights; only one Corrientes lodge includes charter flights from Buenos Aires.
The single room surcharge ranges from US$ 200 per night at a Chubut lodge to 60% of the package (room and boat) at a Corrientes lodge.
A Corrientes lodge charges US$ 650 per night for a non-fishing companion and US$ 950 to fish on arrival or departure day.
A Río Grande lodge requires a non-refundable 50% deposit: cancellation policies vary by operator.

bloques.h: Short answer. The price of a fishing package almost never covers everything. What varies most is whether it includes the license, transfers, flights, single room, and tips, and which extra charges appear (non-fishing companion, fishing on arrival or departure day). Before comparing numbers, compare what each price includes. Below are nine published packages and the questions to ask for a detailed quote.
What each package includes and excludes (published examples)

filas: Double occupancy lodging, all meals, wines, beer and spirits, guide and loaner gear
International and domestic flights, transfers, license, laundry, tips

Single room and boat: +60% (about US$ 4,770 more for the week, our calculation). Non-fishing companion: US$ 650 per night. Fishing on arrival or departure day: US$ 950 (full day) or US$ 750 (half day) per boat
Charter flights between Buenos Aires and the lodge, airport transfers, lodging, meals and alcoholic drinks, guide, license, flies and gear
No extra charges published on the website
Meals and drinks, one guide per two or three anglers, driver and assistant, program vehicles, airport pickup and transfers, licenses and government fees
Tips (paid on final bill), local and international flights, insurance, gear rental, flies
The website mentions both "single occupancy" (in the price) and "double occupancy" (in what’s included): needs confirmation
Transfer from and to San Martín de los Andes airport, shared lodging, meals, alcoholic drinks, guide, loaner gear
International and domestic flights, transfer from Bariloche, licenses, laundry, tips
No extra charges published on the website
Lodging, all meals and drinks, guides (one per two anglers), loaner rods, reels, boots and waders, flies and leader, transfers from and to Esquel or Bariloche airports
Not detailed on the website (license and flights: confirm)
Single room: +US$ 200 per night. Private guide: +US$ 325 per day. Companion: own rate
7 nights, 6 guided fishing days, meals, drinks, transfers from Esquel, licenses and group organization
No extra charges published on the website
Inn in Esquina, 3 nights and 2 days (from US$ 705, group of 2)
Lodging, breakfast, lunch and dinner, drinks, boat, guide, two dozen livebaits per person, 50 liters of fuel and license
Fishing tackle, unless booked in advance
No extra charges published on the website
Onboard lodging and guided fishing days; the website mentions chef-prepared meals, open bar, and loaner gear
Website does not detail license or transfers
Natural bait: ordered on request and charged separately
Day with guide in Bariloche, full day on the Limay (US$ 530)
Private guide and boat, transfers, gear, drinks and lunch (snack for half day)
License managed by the operator: US$ 40 per person per day. El Manso adds US$ 70

bloques.h: Prices and conditions published or reported as of 5 and 6 November 2026, as shown by each operator. Each one charges and groups differently: that’s why the table compares what’s included, not which is better value. Prices for each destination are at how much a golden dorado fishing trip costs and how much a Patagonia trout week costs.
What varies from one package to another?

items: The license: of the nine examples, 4 include it (Itatí, Iberá, Trevelin, and the Esquina inn), 3 leave it out (Corrientes lodge, Neuquén lodge, and the Bariloche day), and 2 don’t specify (Chubut lodges and the boat-hotel). Official rates are at Patagonia fishing license 2026/27 and fishing in Corrientes from Brazil.
The flights: none of the packages that specify include international flights. Only Itatí includes flights, the charters from Buenos Aires; two others explicitly say domestic flights are excluded.

The transfers: some include airport transfers (Iberá, Neuquén from San Martín de los Andes, Chubut from Esquel or Bariloche, Trevelin from Esquel) and others leave it out (Corrientes lodge; in Neuquén, the one departing from Bariloche).

The single room: charged in two ways that aren’t directly comparable: +US$ 200 per night (about US$ 1,400 for a week) at a Chubut lodge and +60% of the package, room and boat, at a Corrientes lodge (about US$ 4,770 for the week). This is our calculation using published rates.
The non-fishing companion: a Corrientes lodge charges US$ 650 per night; Chubut lodges have their own rate. If someone is traveling who won’t fish, this is one of the first things to quote.
Cancellation: a Río Grande lodge requires a non-refundable 50% deposit (fishing Río Grande). We didn’t find most operators’ cancellation policies on their sites: ask for them in writing.

bloques.h: Two ways to book: with an outfitter or direct with an Argentine operator

The lodges in the table are sold through outfitters and fishing agencies that publish per-person rates in dollars, with a list of what’s included and what’s not; some add charter flights from Buenos Aires (Itatí) or transfers (Chubut, Neuquén). Argentine inns and guides who publish prices (the Esquina inn, the Delta boat-hotel, Bariloche guides) do so per group or per person, in dollars or pesos, and usually leave you to arrange travel to the area. We found no reliable data on which route US anglers use more, or which is cheaper: we don’t claim to know. What the examples do show is that not even an "all-inclusive" package covers everything, and that the fishing coordinator doesn’t always handle flights.

filas: Per-person rate and number of nights, list of what’s included and what’s not
Price per group or per person, in dollars or pesos; sometimes "ask for quote"
International flights and, depending on the package, domestic flights and some transfers
Travel to the area and transfer from the airport or border
Who books domestic flights and Buenos Aires nights, who’s responsible if the trip is interrupted, and who you pay for each item
If quoted in dollars or pesos, how to pay, what the license covers, and who picks you up at the airport

bloques.h: How to request a detailed quote

A message that works for any operator: "Hi, I’d like a quote for [dates] for [number] anglers. Can you send a detailed quote showing what’s included and what I need to book separately (license, transfers, flights, Buenos Aires nights, single room, companion, tips), payment and cancellation terms, and what happens if weather or river conditions prevent fishing?"
And these ten questions, before paying a deposit:

items: How many fishing days and how many guided hours are included?
Guide, boat, meals, lodging, transfers, and license: which are included?
Which airport do I arrive at and how is the transfer to the lodge?
Is the fishing private or shared? How many anglers per guide?
What happens if weather, river, or transport interrupt the trip?
How much is the deposit and what are the cancellation and refund policies?
What extra charges are there: tips, laundry, single room, companion?
Can a non-fishing companion come and what does it cost?
What gear can I borrow and what do I need to bring?
How are extras paid and what payment methods are accepted?

bloques.h: What this page doesn’t cover yet
Most operators’ deposit and cancellation policies, insurance and medical evacuation, and details of each flight connection. We’ll add them when verified with a source and date.
Want help comparing? Tell us your dates, group size, and what you want to fish for in the trip form and we’ll send you options with what each includes, no cost or obligation.

paginas.titulo: Fishing gear and rules in Patagonia: felt soles, hooks, and disinfection (2026/27)
paginas.bajada: What the Patagonian regulations say about wading footwear, gear brought into the country, hooks, lead, and fishing hours, with the article for each rule.
paginas.seo_description: Patagonian regulations 2026/27: felt soles, barbed hooks, lead, and non-disinfected gear are banned. Each rule includes its article.
datos: Wading boots with felt soles are prohibited in all waters covered by the Patagonian regulations (art. 22).
Anglers entering the country must use new or disinfected gear (art. 27); guides and outfitters must disinfect gear, boats, and vehicles when required by authorities (art. 28).
In rivers and streams, catch and release is mandatory, with only one single barbless hook or a hook with the barb flattened, and the fish must be released alive (art. 17).
Anchors and sinkers with lead, and lures with lead bodies or heads, are prohibited (art. 22).
The season runs from 1 November 2026 to 1 May 2027; fishing is only allowed during daylight hours and with one rod per angler.

fuentes.nombre: General Regulations for Patagonian Continental Sport Fishing, Part One: articles 6, 7, 15 to 18, 22 and 24 to 28 (text updated 26 October 2026, accessed 6 November 2026)

bloques.h: Short answer. In Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut, and the Southern National Parks, wading boots with felt soles are not allowed, gear brought into the country must be new or disinfected, and in rivers and streams you must use only one single barbless hook and release the fish alive. Anchors and sinkers with lead are also not allowed, nor are lures with a lead body or head. These are rules from the common 2026/27 regulations; each province also has its own annexes.
Can I use boots with felt soles?

No. Article 22 bans "the use of wading boots with felt soles in all waters covered by these regulations," meaning in all four jurisdictions (Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut, and National Parks). Bring wading boots without felt soles.
Do I need to disinfect my gear?

Yes, in two cases. Article 27 states that anglers entering the country are required to use new or disinfected gear. Article 28 requires anglers, guides, and outfitters to disinfect gear, boats, and vehicles whenever and however the authorities require. The regulations do not specify the procedure in these articles.
What hooks and lures can I use?

filas: In rivers and streams, including their sources and mouths in lagoons and lakes and up to 200 meters on both banks, all fish must be released (with exceptions in the annexes)
In mandatory catch and release waters, only one single barbless hook or a hook with the barb flattened; fish must be released alive
Each angler may not use more than one rod at a time
Anchors with lead, lines with lead, sinkers, and lures with lead bodies or heads are prohibited
Chumming is prohibited; fish and clams may not be used as bait where bait is allowed
Entering with carbureted two-stroke engines is prohibited where their use is restricted, even if auxiliary and not in use; four-stroke engines are recommended

bloques.h: When and how much can you fish?

items: Season: from 1 November 2026 to 1 May 2027 inclusive (art. 7), with exceptions in each province’s annexes.
Hours: only during daylight (art. 6).
Lakes and lagoons: one fish per day per angler may be kept between 1 December 2026 and 31 March 2027 (art. 18).
Gravel: it is recommended not to wade fine gravel areas in rivers and streams until 1 January 2027, to avoid damaging spawning beds (art. 24).

bloques.h: License prices are in Patagonia fishing license 2026/27, and dates and closures by area are in when to fish for trout in Patagonia.
What this page does not cover

Santa Cruz and Tierra del Fuego have their own regulations (see the guides for Río Gallegos and Río Grande), and other rules apply in the Litoral (for example, in Corrientes, dorado and surubí must be released). We also do not verify how article 27 is enforced at customs or the disinfection procedure: the regulations only state "new or disinfected." Each province’s annexes may add rules for specific rivers or lakes: check them before fishing a particular water.

paginas.titulo: Fishing license for foreigners in Argentina 2026/27: costs by region
paginas.bajada: 2026/27 rates for non-resident foreign fishing permits in Patagonia, Tierra del Fuego, Santa Cruz, and Corrientes, in pesos and approximate US dollars, and which one you need depending on where you go.
paginas.seo_title: Fishing license for foreigners in Argentina 2026/27
paginas.seo_description: How much is the fishing license for foreigners in Argentina 2026/27: Patagonia, Tierra del Fuego, Santa Cruz, and Corrientes, in pesos and approx. US dollars.
datos: In Patagonia, a non-resident foreigner pays $ 50,000 for one day and $ 280,000 for the season (≈ US$ 32 and ≈ US$ 181).

In Tierra del Fuego, the standard permit costs $ 78,000 for one day and $ 260,000 for the season, and preferred areas (Rivers Grande and Menéndez; Ewan Sur, Irigoyen, and Lake Fagnano) require an additional permit.
In Santa Cruz, it's $ 90,000 for one day and $ 450,000 for the season; in Corrientes, the price is set in liters of “súper” gasoline (approx. $ 35,000 for one day).
Tierra del Fuego and Río Negro have lower rates for foreigners from neighboring countries (for example, Brazilians), with their own conditions.
Dollar amounts are approximate, with US$ 1 = $ 1,545 (xe.com, 8 November 2026): the peso fluctuates, so use the exchange rate of the day.

fuentes.nombre: General Regulations for Patagonian Continental Sport Fishing: permit categories and rates 2026/27 (text updated 26 October 2026)
Resolution S.A. No. 259/2026 of the Secretariat of Environment of Tierra del Fuego (1 October 2026): Annexes I to VI, 2026/2027 season
Santa Cruz Fishing and Aquaculture: permit rates 2026/27 (official portal, read on 4 November 2026)
Provision 1144/2024, Corrientes Directorate of Natural Resources: foreign tourist licenses by liters of “súper” gasoline
Andean Zone Sport Fishing Board: permit for non-resident foreigners from neighboring countries in Río Negro (read on 6 November 2026)

bloques.h: Short answer. There is no national license: each region has its own. For a non-resident foreigner, in 2026/27 it costs $ 50,000 for one day in Patagonia (≈ US$ 32), $ 78,000 in Tierra del Fuego (≈ US$ 50), plus an additional permit if you fish in preferred areas, $ 90,000 in Santa Cruz (≈ US$ 58) and approx. $ 35,000 in Corrientes (≈ US$ 23). A Patagonian permit is valid in four jurisdictions; the other three are only valid in their province.
At a glance: 2026/27 rates for non-resident foreigners

filas: Patagonia (Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut, and National Parks)
3 days: approx. $ 52,000 (≈ US$ 34); 6 days: approx. $ 78,000 (≈ US$ 50)
The tourist annex covers up to 6 days

bloques.h: Rates in pesos are from each region's regulations (see sources), read between 4 and 8 November 2026. Dollar amounts are approximate, with US$ 1 = $ 1,545 according to xe.com on 8 November 2026: the peso fluctuates, so use the exchange rate of the day to pay. Corrientes values are our calculation (liters × price of “súper” gasoline); details are in fishing Corrientes from Brazil.
Which permit do I need depending on where I go?

items: Bariloche, San Martín and Junín de los Andes, Esquel and Trevelin, national parks: the Patagonian permit. Details, validity, and rules in Patagonia fishing license 2026/27.
Río Grande (sea-run trout): the Tierra del Fuego permit and, for preferred areas, an additional permit (below). The Río Grande and Río Gallegos guides have details for each fishery.
Río Gallegos and the rest of Santa Cruz: the Santa Cruz permit, which is processed online on the official portal.
Paso de la Patria, Esquina, Goya, and the rest of Corrientes: the Corrientes foreign tourist license, which is obtained online.
Entre Ríos, Santa Fe, Chaco, Misiones, and the Buenos Aires Delta: each province has its own; we have not included them yet because we have not read their official sources.

bloques.h: Tierra del Fuego: standard permit and additional permit for preferred areas

The standard non-resident foreign permit is shown in the table above. For preferred areas, Resolution 259/2026 also sets an additional permit, with a different rate for residents of neighboring countries such as Brazil:

filas: Rivers Grande and Menéndez, foreigner from neighboring country
Rivers Ewan Sur, Irigoyen, and Lake Fagnano, foreigner
Rivers Ewan Sur, Irigoyen, and Lake Fagnano, foreigner from neighboring country

bloques.h: Our calculation, assuming the additional permit is added to the standard one (the resolution calls it "adicional"): one week on the Grande and Menéndez rivers costs $ 455,000 (≈ US$ 295) for a foreigner and $ 325,000 (≈ US$ 210) for one from a neighboring country. A Río Grande lodge estimates about US$ 550 per angler per week for the license; we do not know what their calculation includes, so it is best to ask them. An oddity in the regulation: the daily permit for neighboring countries in Grande and Menéndez ($ 65,000) is more expensive than the general daily permit ($ 59,000), though for 3 days, a week, and season it is much cheaper; this may be a mistake in the resolution, so confirm with the Secretariat of Environment before paying.

How to get it: the seller registers the angler in the Sport Fishing Information System (siped.ar) and checks the ID; you must carry your ID and proof of payment (or the digital permit from the "pesca deportiva" app) while fishing. To access the Grande River and its tributaries, you must be registered and have a prior reservation in the saptdf.ar access system; the river is open from 30 October 2026 to 18 April 2027, with mandatory catch and release for all salmonids.
Patagonia: unified permit and Río Negro neighboring country permit

A single permit from Neuquén, Río Negro, Chubut, or National Parks is valid in all four jurisdictions. Trolling requires an additional permit ($ 25,000 per day, $ 50,000 for 10 days, and $ 100,000 for the season). Río Negro also sells a 10-day permit for foreigners from neighboring countries at $ 50,000 (≈ US$ 32), valid only in that province. Full details are in Patagonia fishing license 2026/27.
If I go with a lodge or guide, is it included?

It depends on the package: in the nine we compared, the license is included in 4, not included in 3, and 2 do not specify. Ask for it in writing before paying; see what is included in a fishing package in Argentina and what costs extra.
What this page does not cover yet

Licenses for Entre Ríos, Santa Fe, Chaco, Misiones, and Buenos Aires; additional trolling permits for Tierra del Fuego and Santa Cruz; and the neighboring country permit for Chubut, which appears in a secondary list and not in an official source we have read. We will add them when we verify them with a source and a date.
